opinions.title: GRGBANKING (002152.SZ): Operating performance under slight pressure, with AI capabilities seeing accelerated adoption across multiple scenarios
opinions.opi_all: {"description":"CSC*A-share listed company brief analysis*GRGBANKING (002152.SZ): Operating performance under slight pressure, with AI capabilities seeing accelerated adoption across multiple scenarios*002152*Computer*YING Ying,ZHANG Min*Buy*20260915 Key takeaway The company released its 1H26 results. In 1H26, operating revenue reached RMB5.124bn, down 2.86% YoY; net profit attributable to shareholders of the parent company was RMB423mn, down 9.16% YoY; and net profit attributable to shareholders of the parent company excluding non-recurring gains and losses was RMB380mn, down 6.21% YoY. In 2Q26, revenue reached RMB2.912bn, down 6.81% YoY; net profit attributable to shareholders of the parent company was RMB197mn, down 12.57% YoY; and net profit attributable to shareholders of the parent company excluding non-recurring gains and losses was RMB173mn, down 11.36% YoY. The core fintech business remained stable, with traditional strengths and digital finance innovation advancing in tandem. Revenue from intelligent equipment declined, but overseas orders and intelligent product upgrades are expected to support a subsequent recovery. AI vertical models and agents are gradually entering industry-specific scenarios, while the cross-border payment license and digital renminbi business are expected to create incremental growth opportunities over the medium to long term. We maintain our “Buy” rating. Event On August 28, the company released its 1H26 results. In 1H26, operating revenue reached RMB5.124bn, down 2.86% YoY; net profit attributable to shareholders of the parent company was RMB423mn, down 9.16% YoY; and net profit attributable to shareholders of the parent company excluding non-recurring gains and losses was RMB380mn, down 6.21% YoY. Quick Take Earnings under slight pressure, with a significant marginal improvement in cash flow in 2Q26. In 1H26, the company recorded operating revenue of RMB5.124bn, down 2.86% YoY; net profit attributable to shareholders of the parent company of RMB423mn, down 9.16% YoY; and net profit attributable to shareholders of the parent company excluding non-recurring gains and losses of RMB380mn, down 6.21% YoY, while its overall gross margin was 28.88%, up 0.44 pct YoY. In 2Q26, operating revenue reached RMB2.912bn, down 6.81% YoY; net profit attributable to shareholders of the parent company was RMB197mn, down 12.57% YoY; and net profit attributable to shareholders of the parent company excluding non-recurring gains and losses was RMB173mn, down 11.36% YoY, while gross margin was 26.86%, up 0.10 pct YoY. Net cash flow from operating activities was negative RMB936mn in 1H26, while 2Q26 recorded a net inflow of RMB222mn, turning positive YoY and indicating a marginal improvement in operating cash flow. The core fintech business remained stable, with traditional strengths and digital finance innovation advancing in tandem. In 1H26, the company’s fintech business generated revenue of RMB2.798bn, down 2.22% YoY and accounting for 54.60% of total revenue; gross margin was 32.66%, down 0.95 pct YoY. The company has ranked first in China’s smart financial equipment market by market share for 18 consecutive years. Its financial equipment technical services now cover more than 350,000 units. During the reporting period, it won bids for projects from national banks including ICBC, CCB, and PSBC. It also made breakthroughs in head-office-level projects, including smart displays for Bank of China and smart electronic locks and mobile banking outreach solutions for China Bohai Bank. In digital public finance, CTJ applies AI technology to core public finance scenarios such as financial and accounting supervision and performance management, based on its vertical large model for public finance.
